channel.title: The Colorado Sun - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Colorado Sun (coloradosun.com)

item.title: Why your Colorado property tax bill still increased this year
item.description: The state had granted temporary tax discounts in recent years, but they are expiring. At the same time, tax rates paid to schools are also effectively increasing.

item.title: Littwin: I flew as far away as I could, only to return to the same Trump-infected place
item.description: Columnist Mike Littwin writes that when he returned from a trip to Antartica, he arrived just in time for a lesson in what it really means to be an American.

item.title: Trump administration targets Colorado, other Democratic-led states for health and transportation grant fund clawback
item.description: Among the programs set to lose funding in Colorado is one that focuses on HIV prevention and treatment

item.title: Legislature rejects attempt to let Colorado communities increase taxes on often-vacant homes
item.description: House Bill 1036, geared toward addressing the housing shortage in resort communities, would have let the revenue generated by the new taxes pay for affordable housing projects

item.title: Grand jury refuses to indict Jason Crow, other Democratic lawmakers over video about illegal military orders
item.description: Grand jury rejections are extraordinarily unusual, but have happened repeatedly in recent months in Washington as citizens who have heard the government’s evidence have come away underwhelmed in a number of cases

item.title: Aurora selects final site for its largest reservoir yet in Park County. Will it fill up?
item.description: The proposed Wild Horse Reservoir is set for a site near Spinney Mountain Reservoir in Park County near the town of Hartsel.

item.title: Gunnison Valley community rallies behind family after 7-year-old boy attacked, killed by dog
item.description: The Feb. 4 attack has left a tight-knit Western Slope community reeling. Police remain tight-lipped as the investigation continues.

item.title: Colorado law prohibits candidates from running for two elected offices at the same time. Sort of.
item.description: Candidates sometimes simultaneously maintain campaign accounts for state and federal office, or state and municipal office, when their pursuit of those jobs overlaps. Technically, they are running for two positions at once. Practically, they are not, and state elections officials don’t treat it as a violation of the law.

item.title: The Michelin Guide expands to cover all of Colorado in 2026
item.description: The premier restaurant guide landed in Colorado in 2023 to focus on four major culinary scenes. This year, the anonymous agents will scour the whole state.

item.title: Colorado forced to share personal Medicaid data with Trump administration, including ICE
item.description: Denver Health told Medicaid patients that “limited” personal information could be shared with U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement.
